# ALL Feature Ledger

This file tracks implemented features/fixes with implementation date.

## 2026-09-09
- Templates Phase 1: Added template engine, template registry, declarative template specs, and built-in templates (Python Script, Python CLI, Python Package).
- Templates UI: Added Templates menu, template preview, and project creation wizard integrated with PES environment/package services.
- Templates Phase 1.1: Added non-blocking create workflow with window minimize, creation-state tracking, success/failure handling, and open-project flow.
- Project open workflow: Added reusable launcher path using existing open_with detection/configuration and preferred editor persistence.

## 2026-09-10
- Configuration/Preferences (Tools -> Configuration): added centralized user configuration UI and service for default venv path, default Python selection, default package manager (pip/uv with availability checks), default project tool, template project defaults (create venv/init git), appearance mode, UI scaling, apply/save/cancel/reset flows, and runtime refresh integration.
- Backfill (existing core UI capabilities): environment create/delete, one-click activation, package management (install/update/uninstall), vulnerability scanner + insights, environment search/rename, recent usage tracking, environment-size visibility, and requirements import/export.

## 2026-09-26
- Per-environment package-update monitoring: added a default-off creation opt-in, SQLite cached update counts with a six-hour TTL, asynchronous startup checks using the configured pip/uv package-manager path, and Updates table states for disabled, checking, checked, and unavailable environments.
- Package-update cache consistency: successful pip/uv installs, uninstalls, upgrades, and requirements imports now invalidate the per-environment result; GUI completion refreshes the row and starts a fresh opted-in check.
- Compact environment creation UI: moved creation controls into an on-demand, reusable dialog with screen-aware sizing, scrollable content, and explicit focus/z-order handling.
- Environment update shortcut: double-clicking an Updates cell toggles automatic checking for only that environment; the usage guide documents the shortcut.
- Application updates: Help → Check for Updates compares the installed distribution with PyPI, offers confirmed pip installation and restart, handles frozen builds via the release page, and About now reports the installed package version.
- Backfill (existing interaction UX): environment table shortcuts including double-click activation and one-click copy of recent location to clipboard with Open At prefill behavior.
- Backfill (existing UI personalization): appearance mode switching (Light/Dark/System) and runtime UI scaling controls.
- Backfill (existing extensibility): plugin system with plugin discovery, enable/disable lifecycle, persisted plugin state, startup/shutdown hooks, scan-complete hook, and plugin manager UI.
- Backfill (existing CLI capabilities): environment operations via flags (`--create`, `--delete`, `--list`, `--install`, `--uninstall`, `--export`, `--import-reqs`) plus runtime/project subcommands (`init`, `on`, `off`, `status`, `list-projects`, `run`).
- Backfill (existing runtime management): project metadata/registry persistence (`pes.config`, global registry), managed-environment tracking, and preferred package-manager integration for runtime execution flows.
- Backfill (existing package-manager architecture): unified package manager routing with per-environment pip/uv selection and automatic pip fallback when uv is unavailable or a uv operation fails.
- Backfill (existing reliability): AutoResolver for pip/uv install failures with conflict detection, version-constraint stripping fallback, and bounded retry attempts.
- Backfill (existing analysis backend): dependency impact preview backend module for pre-install change analysis (additions/upgrades/removals, conflicts, and potential breaking changes).
- Templates Phase 1.2: Added Manage Templates lifecycle for user templates (Add/Use/Delete) from Local Project and GitHub repository import.
- Security and import controls: Added centralized exclusion/sensitive-file filters, GitHub URL validation, safe clone handling, and temporary clone cleanup.
- Registry/Engine unification: User templates are discovered by the same registry and generated by the same template engine as built-in templates.
- Template metadata workflow: Added template preview before save, auto-generated editable template IDs, source metadata capture, and optional project-name token replacement for imported templates.
- Project open UX hardening: Added detected-app selection dialog, preferred editor reuse, and retry/choose-another recovery flow when opening a created project fails.
- Template-plugin integration: Added `after_template_created` hook execution with project/template context and safe error logging.
- Fix: GitHub import now defaults template name to actual repository slug (for example fastapi-starter-kit) instead of temporary clone folder name.
- Vulnerability dashboard remediation: Added per-vulnerability `Update Now` and environment-wide `Upgrade all Packages` actions. They apply remediation-recommended fixed versions after confirmation, run without blocking the UI, persist fixed status, and refresh the report with partial-failure feedback.
- Templates Phase 1.3: Added GitHub-backed Community Templates discovery with asynchronous metadata search, categories, sorting, pagination, lightweight caching, static repository preview, duplicate-origin detection, and import through the existing user-template storage, registry, and project-creation workflow. Community repositories remain untrusted and are never executed during discovery, preview, or import.

## 2026-09-23
- Release 2.1.0: bumped the version in `pyproject.toml`, `py_env_studio/config.ini`, and `docs/conf.py`, added `docs/releases/v2.1.0.md` (major updates: templates, configuration center, Python Install Manager runtime, remediation actions, native charts, progress gauges, MCP beta) and marked v2.0.8 as superseded.
- MCP declared beta: documented the exposed status in the CLI help, the plugin/hook docs, and every MCP reference; added a dedicated `docs/reference/mcp.md` with client setup, tool list, settings, security notes, and troubleshooting; added the `[mcp]` section (enabled/server_name/transport/log_level) to the packaged `config.ini`.
- Documentation refresh: updated the CLI reference (`--activate`, `--gui`, managed-project subcommands, MCP beta), the usage manual (Templates menu, Configuration, Plugins, runtime-managed projects, MCP beta, native charts wording), the installation guide (requirements, verify, GUI launch, extras, uninstall), the architecture page (MCP, project intelligence, project contract, runtime providers, status bar), contributing (dev setup, tests, Sphinx docs build, release checklist), and the plugin docs (18 hooks including `after_template_created`, corrected paths).
- PluginHook gained `AFTER_TEMPLATE_CREATED` so the documented template hook is part of the public hook enumeration (the UI already emitted it).
- Removed the stale MkDocs `site/` build output; the docs pipeline is Sphinx/Furo via `.readthedocs.yaml`.

## 2026-09-18
- Window icon fix: every Py Env Studio window (all CustomTkinter dialogs, plugin windows and the Vulnerability Insights Dashboard) now shows the PES application icon. Added shared icon helpers (resolve, apply, delayed re-apply) plus a global Tk window hook that covers windows created later, and reused the same resolver for the Windows Start Menu shortcut.
- Charts migration: the Vulnerability Insights Dashboard no longer uses matplotlib. The severity breakdown and trend charts are now native tkinter-dash widgets (BarChart / LineChart) rendered straight into the CustomTkinter bottom panel, with a placeholder label when a package has no scan history, dark/light theming matched to the active appearance mode, and duplicate trend labels de-duplicated. matplotlib was replaced by tkinter-dash in pyproject.toml / requirements.txt, the PyInstaller specs now bundle the icon resources and tkinter_dash, and tests/test_vulnerability_insights_charts.py covers the migration.
